subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cos(2 Tan⁻¹(1/7)) = sin(4 Tan⁻¹(1/3)).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.74 — SAQ chapter 12 Inverse Trig Functions, answer 78.2. Printed appearances: none — this answer carries no year tag. The twin of 78.1, with a FOUR on the right instead of a two. sin4β is handled as sin(2(2β)) — the double-angle formula applied twice, with tan2β computed in between. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: this same chapter DOES print 1+1+1+1 against answer 77 on book p.73, so the shape is the chapter's own, and the weightings here follow it. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. ONE PRESENTATION CHOICE, made deliberately: the book draws a small right triangle beside each answer that needs a second ratio (for example sinα = 4/5 giving cosα = 3/5). Those are authored here as the one-line algebraic step instead, with the triangle route named in the margin note — it keeps the nine answers consistent and avoids three near-identical figures where the algebra is a single line. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q16 is the Inverse Trig Functions slot. NOTE: Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-ONLY unit — the paper gives it no Section-A and no Section-C slot, and this book has no Inverse Trig LAQ chapter (LAQ chapters are 1-6) and no VSAQ chapter (VSAQ chapters are 14-19). The same shape as Unit 7. Verified by walking to p.75, where SAQ chapter 13 Properties of Triangles begins.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order, and say which formula you reach for and why.

steps.label: Evaluate the left side
steps.margin_note: First mark. Identical left side to the twin, and it gives the same 24/25.
steps.memory_tip: cos 2α = (1 − tan²α)/(1 + tan²α) takes tanα directly: (1 − 1/49)/(1 + 1/49) = 24/25.

recall.must_convey: That the left side is cos2α with tanα = 1/7, giving 24/25.
accept: the left side is cos two alpha which comes to twenty four over twenty five as before
same left hand side as the twin, twenty four twenty fifths
evaluate cos two alpha with tan alpha one seventh
left side twenty four by twenty five, twin lantidi
the left hand side is twenty four over twenty five

steps.why: The left side is word for word the twin question, so its value is already known — only the right side is new.
common_mistakes: Recomputing it differently and getting a mismatch.

steps.label: Find tan2β first
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. sin4β cannot be reached in one step. Compute tan2β first — then 4β is just 2(2β) and the same formula applies again.
steps.memory_tip: sin 4β cannot be reached in one step. Get tan 2β first, then treat 4β as 2(2β).

recall.must_convey: That tan2β is computed first as 3/4, so that 4β can be treated as 2(2β).
accept: find tan two beta first which is three quarters then four beta is two times two beta
compute tan of double beta before going to four beta
tan two beta comes to three by four
modata tan two beta kanukovali, three by four vasthundi
get tan two beta so the formula can be applied again

steps.why: There is no formula for sin4θ in terms of tanθ directly. Stepping through tan2θ is what makes the second application possible.
common_mistakes: Trying to double the angle twice in one line.
Using the sin2θ formula where the tan2θ one is needed.

steps.label: Evaluate sin4β and compare
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Now sin4β = sin(2(2β)) uses the same tangent form, with tan2β = 3/4 — which is exactly the twin question’s β, so the answer is the same 24/25.
steps.memory_tip: Use tan 2β = 3/4, not tanβ, in the final formula. Then state that both sides are 24/25.

recall.must_convey: That sin4β is evaluated as sin(2(2β)) using tan2β = 3/4, giving 24/25, and that both sides are then stated equal.
accept: sin four beta is sin of two times two beta which with tan two beta three quarters gives twenty four over twenty five so both sides agree
apply the formula again to get twenty four twenty fifths and compare
both sides equal twenty four over twenty five so it is proved
sin four beta kuda twenty four by twenty five vasthundi, rendu equal
the right side matches the left

steps.why: tan2β came out as 3/4 — exactly the tangent in the twin question. That is why both twins land on the same number, and it is not a coincidence.
common_mistakes: Using tanβ instead of tan2β in the final formula.
Never stating that the two sides agree.

insider_note: The right side is 4Tan⁻¹, so find tan2β = 3/4 first and treat sin4β as sin(2 · 2β). Reaching for a quadruple-angle formula is far longer and rarely lands.
